title: Optimal Welfare and Policy Regret with Unknown Latent Response Groups
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope. D0.5 math pass with no findings and verified citation; independent validity gate confirms no bounded field repair; paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: Its scope remains exactly two shared response profiles, known uniform labels, fair randomization, and bounded component proportions; inclusion transfers only lower bounds to broader discrete models.

The arbitrary-accuracy computation theorem supplies a terminating exhaustive construction without an efficiency guarantee, while the executed program collapses every nonzero count into one tail state and the informative calibration at lambda 256 remains a broad analytic bracket.

These restrictions, limited informative computation, and an indirect connection to the [tlverse workflow](https://tlverse.org/tlverse-handbook/dynamic-and-optimal-individualized-treatment-regimes.html) constrain the projected paper score, although the framing does not overclaim broader-class sharpness or an exact positive-intensity optimizer.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived matched value and policy rates, a learned-fiber critical risk transfer, certified arbitrary-accuracy computation, and a total original-record sharp attaining procedure on the supplied two-archetype benchmark. D0.5 mathematics passed with no findings after publisher-source verification, but the delivered paper was capped at subfield (score ceiling 6.6 below the 7.4 field threshold) due to restricted scope, inefficient computation, limited informative calibration, and indirect applied reach. The independent validity gate found no bounded same-scope field repair; F-stage Lean formalization did not run.
tldr: Unknown response grouping can make optimal welfare easier to estimate than a personalized treatment rule is to implement. On the complete randomized categorical two-profile benchmark with unknown feasible proportions, the proved headline value MSE frontier is \(\min\{1,d^{2/3}/n\}\); a separate benchmark corollary gives policy regret \(\min\{1,\sqrt{d/n}\}\). A legal common-pair witness shows that full first and second mark tensors do not identify welfare, whereas triples do. At \(n\asymp d^{2/3}\), original-record minimax risk converges compact-uniformly to the full marked-triple decision game through learned lower-moment fibers. A total data-only procedure attains that sharp limit, and certified continuum decision programs compute it to arbitrary accuracy with lower witnesses and upper-guarantee rules. The exact zero-intensity risk is \(1/1024\), with a certified informative continuum improvement at positive intensity. Generic third-view identification, cubic merger geometry and policy-regret ancestry are credited. Original-class value-risk converses transfer to the larger discrete benchmark classes by inclusion; the upper guarantees and sharp frontier remain specific to the declared two-profile class.
gap: Zeng et al., version 3, Discussion 8, the displayed formula \(\mu_{ak}=\mu_{a,g(k)}\) and its surrounding paragraph, explicitly motivate a small number of known or unknown response groups; the later estimand-extension paragraph names optimal treatment regimes. They do not establish the exact two-profile restriction or the value frontier here. Existing grouped-mixture identification and consistency do not determine sharp welfare risk when grouping is revealed through rare categorical repeats and lower tensors must be learned. Their standard treatment positivity condition is distinct from the full labelled support maintained by this benchmark design.
fill: The headline value-risk frontier and compact-uniform learned-fiber critical limit quantify oracle-welfare precision. A separate policy-regret benchmark corollary supplies the implementation comparison. Uniform fiber transport, strict pair-information non-representability, and informative continuum calibration support the sharp procedures and certified decision programs posed as explicit open questions.
